claims.claim: EMCOR sits at the skilled-trade execution layer connecting electrical/mechanical systems and industrial/building infrastructure to data-network, water, healthcare and institutional demand; this makes labor availability, project execution and customer capital spending the key bottleneck chain.

Q2 RPO growth was broad across Network and Communications, Water and Wastewater, Institutional and Healthcare rather than presented as a single-market dependency, improving scenario breadth while not eliminating project-cycle risk.

causalEdges: infrastructure/data/water/health demand -> complex MEP projects -> skilled trades/project management -> commissioned capacity -> human/economic services
skilled-labor/material constraints -> execution capacity -> schedule/margin -> realized project value
diverse sector RPO -> workload visibility -> execution demand

risks.risk: Skilled-labor scarcity, materials constraints and project complexity can shift a demand bottleneck into an execution bottleneck.

unknowns.unknown: Customer-level concentration and exact data-center share are not disclosed in the cited Q2 release.

claims.claim: Record $17.14B RPO supports workload visibility but is not equivalent to guaranteed revenue or margin; timing, cancellations, scope changes, labor and cost execution remain the correct falsifiers.
Q2 revenue growth of 19.8% was reported as 19.6% organic after acquisition and UK-sale adjustments, reducing the concern that headline growth was primarily acquisition-manufactured in this quarter.

risks.risk: RPO can overstate economic certainty if project timing, scope or margins change before conversion.
Raised guidance increases the execution bar; sustained margin expansion must be verified against labor and project-mix pressure.

unknowns.unknown: No material present accounting or governance contradiction was established in this pass; customer concentration remains a non-gating unknown.
